title: The Crash Impact Signature Database — Overview: the Signature impact doctrine
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature impact doctrine treats every crash as a budget: so many kilojoules arrive, and the structure must spend them all before they reach the occupant. The doctrine's first law is that the occupant never pays — structure, foam, and distance pay first. Its second law is that the pulse is the product: peak deceleration matters more than total crush. Signature records develop these ideas into original analysis methods, original absorption concepts, and original test philosophies, all labeled as Signature originals.
capabilities: The energy budget: kilojoules must be spent before the occupant
First law: the occupant never pays
Second law: the pulse is the product
Original methods, honestly labeled

title: The Crash Impact Signature Database — Signature collision analysis
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature collision analysis method reconstructs impacts backwards: from the rest positions and crush depths, it walks the energy ledger in reverse to estimate the closing speed. Crush depth is read like a receipt — each centimeter of permanent deformation is energy spent — and the ledger must balance within the method's stated uncertainty. The analysis is taught as a worked discipline with checklists, because a method that only its inventor can run is a trick, not a tool.
capabilities: Backwards reconstruction from rest positions
Crush depth as an energy receipt
The energy ledger and its stated uncertainty
Checklist-taught method, not inventor magic

title: The Crash Impact Signature Database — Signature absorption design
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature absorption design philosophy shapes structure like a story with three acts: the sacrificial nose that spends the first energy cheaply, the programmed rails that meter the middle, and the unyielding cell that refuses the ending. Each act has a force corridor — a band the crush force must stay inside — and the design is drawn as corridors first, metal second. Foam and honeycomb are cast as supporting characters with one job: constant force, no drama.
capabilities: Three-act structure: sacrifice, meter, refuse
Force corridors drawn before metal
Foam and honeycomb in supporting roles
The unyielding cell as the final act

title: The Crash Impact Signature Database — Signature test philosophy
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature test philosophy crashes what must be crashed and simulates what can be simulated: full-scale tests are spent on the unknown unknowns, simulation covers the knowns. Every physical test is designed to answer one question, written down before the run, and the report opens with whether the question was answered. A test that answers nothing is filed as waste, however spectacular the footage. Simulation earns its keep by predicting a test before it runs — prediction first, then the crash, then the comparison.
capabilities: Crash the unknowns, simulate the knowns
One question per test, written before the run
Waste filing: spectacle without answers
Prediction-first simulation discipline

demo.title: Question-answer ledger
demo.code: const tests=[{q:'rail buckle mode',answered:true},{q:'foam density',answered:true},{q:'paint color',answered:false}];const waste=tests.filter(t=>!t.answered);J({total:tests.length,waste:waste.length});assert(waste.length===1,'ledger');

title: The Crash Impact Signature Database — Signature material doctrine
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature material doctrine grades materials by their manners in a crash: how they behave when surprised. Ductile metals bow and stay standing; brittle ones shatter without warning; composites delaminate in layers like pages. The doctrine's catalog records each material's crash manners — yield, hardening, tear, and the temperature where courage fails — and its selection rule is blunt: never let a brittle material guard a human. Warmth is a design input, not an afterthought.
capabilities: Crash manners: how materials behave when surprised
Ductile bows, brittle shatters, composites delaminate
The temperature where courage fails
Selection rule: no brittle guardians

title: The Crash Impact Signature Database — Signature simulation doctrine
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature simulation doctrine simulates to decide, not to decorate: every model exists to choose between designs, and a model that cannot change a decision is deleted. Mesh studies are mandatory — the answer must not depend on the mesh — and the doctrine requires the coarsest mesh that still decides correctly, because compute is a budget too. Validation is a public ritual: the model predicts, the test happens, and the comparison is published inside the database, misses included.
capabilities: Simulate to decide, not to decorate
Mandatory mesh independence studies
Coarsest deciding mesh: compute is a budget
Public validation ritual, misses included

title: The Crash Impact Signature Database — Signature occupant doctrine
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature occupant doctrine designs from the human outward: the survivable pulse is drawn first — what deceleration a body can take, for how long — and the structure is then shaped to deliver exactly that pulse. Restraint systems are choreographed with the crush: the belt pays out, the airbag stages, the seat strokes, all timed to the milliseconds of the crash. The doctrine's measure is not the star rating but the stranger test: would you put someone you love in the seat?
capabilities: Design from the human outward
The survivable pulse drawn first
Choreographed restraints timed to milliseconds
The stranger test as the final measure

title: The Crash Impact Signature Database — Signature barrier doctrine
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature barrier doctrine treats the static object as a design partner, not just a wall: guardrails are shaped to redirect rather than stop, bollards are spaced to catch without spearing, and deformable faces are tuned to the vehicles they expect. The doctrine catalogs barriers by the question they ask — who do you protect, and from what — and requires every barrier design to name its protected party first. A barrier that protects the wall instead of the human has failed its doctrine.
capabilities: Barriers as design partners: redirect, not just stop
Bollard spacing: catch without spearing
Every barrier names its protected party first
The protected-human test for barrier designs
